about: Every part of the pitaya harness: its level, what it requires first, what it works better with, and what it needs from the project. A level includes every component at or below it; there is no custom selection. levels.md is generated from this file, and tests check the dependencies against the recipes.

needs.github: A GitHub repository, so rulesets and required checks exist
needs.tickets: Every agent PR comes from a ticket, on a branch named ticket/<id>-<slug>: docs/tickets/T-<nnn>.md files (recommended, optionally mirrored by issues) or issues (/plan writes tickets, /build names branches)
needs.ticket-scope: Each ticket lists the paths it may change under "## Scope"
needs.ticket-test-ids: Each ticket names one test per completion condition under "## Test IDs"
needs.junit-xml: The test command can write JUnit XML

components.summary: A failing test before the code, one behaviour at a time
"Done" comes with commands, real output and the model's name
A roadmap of milestones, then each milestone cut into tickets with conditions and scope, approved by the Owner
One ticket, one branch, one PR, red then green
A fresh subagent re-runs the work and posts PASS or FAIL
A summary of merged work for the Owner, every claim linked to evidence
Unclear or risky decisions go to the Owner with options instead of a guess
Where the project stands and the next command, or how to do something; read only
Installs the chosen files without overwriting anything, and writes the harness file
The config every skill reads first: Owner, machine account, test command, tickets, level
The map every agent tool starts from; CLAUDE.md makes Claude Code read it
The project's words, its module map, and what earlier work learned the hard way
The Owner's decisions in one place, append only
Read denied on secrets, git denied `--output` and the like; hooks block main pushes and wipes, ask on rule edits, merges
The test command, written once in a script, and the workflow that runs it on every PR
A ruleset: changes reach main only through PRs, tests must pass, only the Owner merges
Notes that let another session take over stopped work
An optional review for the Owner, turned on in the harness file
Repeated mistakes become proposed rules with an enforcer, and spent guardrails get retired
Scenarios first, then interfaces, data flow, notifications and state owners; tickets come from the scenarios
One GitHub account per agent role, with Write access only
Every commit in a PR is authored by the expected machine account
A PR changes only the paths its ticket lists
Rules, specs and CI can't change in a ticket PR unless the ticket names the file
Every test that passes on the base still exists and passes
Every completion condition has a test that exists and passes
Listed files only gain lines
Only one ticket at a time changes a migration, lockfile or other shared resource
A project skill that drives the real app as a user would, with evidence
Only with several agent accounts: CODEOWNERS, so only the Owner's approval counts
A PR without an evidence section, or a UI change without screenshots, can't merge
Runs the active milestone: hands tickets to fresh builders and verifiers, merges when allowed, stops at Owner gates
A start-up routine and a feature list where agents may only mark items as passing
Another model reviews sensitive or risky PRs
Agents merge ticket PRs into milestone branches on another session's PASS for the head; the Owner merges main
Risk tags, interrogation of high-risk PRs, a swarm and a log audit per milestone, an arena for contested designs
A task set drawn from real failures, run before and after a harness change
